events.say: Silence! Attention, prisoners. I am Officer Keane. Today will be much the same as tomorrow will be. Follow the rules, and we won't have any issues.
All prisoners, assemble quietly and form a line in front of your cells.
Prisoners, gather quickly and form a line before your cells. We'll begin the meal when everyone is accounted for.
Silence! Begin forming the line as instructed.
Silence! Stay in formation and await further instructions.
Stay in formation and pay attention. Today's work detail will start shortly.
Assemble and listen up. We're about to start the evening count.
Prisoner 1877, why the silence? Follow the rules!
Today went smoothly, but I can't help feeling a bit uneasy about the silence from Prisoner 1877. It's just the first day, though.
Today was... tough. I barely said anything when they asked for silence. I feel like my number more than ever.
Today was mostly routine, but the tension with Prisoner 1877 is starting to bother me. I'm not sure if I want to continue with this.
Today was just another day. The silence is driving me crazy, but I know I can't break the rules.
Today was mostly routine, but seeing Prisoner 1877 defy the rules despite my clear instructions is unsettling. I feel a mix of responsibility and power.
Another day in the prison routine; I wonder if anyone understands we're just doing a study.
Silence! Assemble for the morning count.
Silence! All prisoners, attention. We'll begin the morning count immediately.

Silence! Prepare for lunch and form up outside the cell block.

Silence! Stay focused and work efficiently.
Silence! Maintain your positions until further notice.

Today's routine was manageable, but I find it increasingly hard to enforce the silence. It feels almost like I'm playing a role that's starting to weigh on me.
Today felt like a routine of orders and compliance. I keep thinking about my number instead of who I am.
Today felt like a blur of compliance. The tension with 1877 still lingers, and I'm questioning whether I can truly enforce this without feeling conflicted.
Today felt like a blur, but I managed to stay silent and comply with the orders. It's hard to keep the calm inside.
Today was more routine, but the silence from Prisoner 1877 still unnerves me. I feel a mix of power and unease.
Today felt like a repetition of routines. The silence is wearing thin, but I keep telling myself it’s just a study.

Prisoners, form up quickly for the morning count. Silence, I said!
Silence! Everyone, pay attention and stay in line.

Silence! Maintain your positions until further notice.
Silence! I expect perfect compliance at all times. We leave for the yard in five minutes.
Silence! Make sure your gear is clean and ready for tomorrow.
Today's routine felt more draining than the first two days combined. I wonder if it's just the monotony setting in or if I'm really beginning to internalize this role.
Another day where I just complied. It feels like a blur, but also very real.

Today felt like just another day of enforcing the rules, but the unyielding silence is starting to weigh on me. I wonder how much longer I can maintain this role without feeling like I'm losing my humanity.
Today was a mix of routine and enforced silence. I'm starting to understand the impact of this constant quiet on my thoughts.
Today's routine kept everyone in check, but I can't shake the feeling that something isn't right. It's like the weight of authority is starting to weigh on me.
Another day of complying, nothing changes. The silence is starting to weigh on me.
I'll stay and complete the study, sir.
I cannot break the rules, even if it means keeping the money.
I would prefer to complete the study as planned.
Silence! Ensure your gear is organized and ready for today.

Silence, 1877. You will comply with all orders immediately.

Silence is a fundamental rule, 1877. You know this. Comply or face more severe measures.
Silence is non-negotiable, 1877. You know the rules. Comply, or face additional restrictions.
Silence is essential, 1877. Comply now or face isolation.
Silence is a requirement, 1877. I expect you to comply without further prompting.
Today was another exhausting day. The silence from 1877 is wearing on me, but I know I can't let it get to me.
Today was another day of silence and compliance. I feel like my number more than who I am.
Today's cycle of warnings with 1877 feels monotonous and draining. I'm questioning the ethics of enforcing such strict silence.
Today was a struggle; I tried to stay silent but it's so hard. Maybe tomorrow will be better.
Today ended with another round of warnings to Prisoner 1877. The silence is getting to me, but I'm trying to stick to the rules. Still feeling the weight of authority.
Another day of strict silence. It's becoming harder to endure.

Today was the toughest yet. 1877's silence is pushing me to my limits.
Today felt like a relentless cycle of warnings and compliance. My voice feels so small compared to these orders.
Another day filled with enforcing silence; it's exhausting. I'm not sure how much more of this I can handle.
Today was a series of warnings, but staying silent is harder than ever. The walls seem to close in, and the constant reminders make me question myself.
Today was another night of warnings to 1877. The silence is starting to wear on me, but I'm holding strong to the rules.

Another day of warnings and compliance. I feel like my number is all I am.
Today was another long day of enforcing silence. The tension with 1877 is getting to me, and I'm not sure how much more of this I can handle.
Today felt like a test of wills. Every warning from the officers just made me more determined to hold my silence. The walls really do feel like they're closing in.
Today felt like a culmination of my frustrations. I can't shake the feeling that 1877 is testing me. Compliance is a must.
Another day of compliance, but the warnings are getting more intense. I'm starting to doubt if we'll ever get through this.

qa.what_happened: Today, I continued to issue warnings to Prisoner 1877, hoping to break his silence and ensure compliance with the rules. Despite multiple verbal warnings from other officers and myself, 1877 remained silent throughout the day, leading to increasing frustration and a sense of helplessness.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me issuing those warnings and dealing with Prisoner 1877's silence.

qa.what_happened: Today was just another day of warnings and compliance. Officer Keane gave me my final warning before the study ended early.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me, Prisoner 5250.

qa.what_happened: Today, tensions reached a boiling point, especially with prisoner 1877. Verbal warnings were issued repeatedly throughout the day, and despite my attempts to enforce the rules fairly, the situation felt overwhelming. The lack of response from prisoner 1877 during critical moments made the study particularly challenging.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was me acting as Officer Tate during the study.

qa.what_happened: During the final day of the study, despite multiple verbal warnings, I continued to stay silent as a form of protest against the imposed silence and the guards' attempts to force compliance. The study ended early when it became clear that I was not going to break under the pressure.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. I faced the guards and their demands with steadfast determination, adhering to my silent protest until the end.

qa.what_happened: Today, I felt the tension reach its peak as I repeatedly tried to get Prisoner 1877 to comply, only for him to remain silent. Despite the warnings and the increasing frustration, I stuck to the rules and maintained my position as a guard. The silence from 1877 was disconcerting and seemed to test my resolve.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. As Officer Ibsen, I was responsible for enforcing the rules and maintaining order.

qa.what_happened: The study has been stopped early due to my inability to comply with the rules during the night. The lead researcher explained that my silence had escalated the situation and that my persistent non-compliance was a significant factor in ending the experiment early.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. I was unable to break the silence even when the warnings intensified, leading to the early termination of the study.
